findings.title: Review provider failure now returns a result with a misleading "unexpected error" log
findings.description:
The `except ProviderError` branch used to re-raise into `execute`'s catch-all. It now returns `_exception_result(...)` itself. It also logs `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error in step %s")` for what is a named provider failure. The branch has already logged a WARNING with the artifact path. The result is a second, differently worded record of one failure, with a full traceback for an expected error. Dispatch and summary deliberately log named provider failures as a single ERROR line with no traceback (issue 200). Use `_logger.error` with the message, or drop the extra log.

Two related risks in the same handler:
- `effort_sent_by_profile()` at line 491 calls `get_profile` and `ensure_provider_loaded`. If either raises, it replaces the original `ProviderError` and no usage record is written. Resolve it defensively, or compute it before the `try`.
- The handler now returns a failed `ActionResult` for a part. I did not verify that the split-review caller treats a failed part the same way it treated the earlier raise (aborting the remaining parts). Confirm this in `_review` / the parts loop.

findings.title: `sq stats reviews --json` prints plain text when the directory is missing
findings.description: `report.missing_dir` is checked before `as_json`, so `--json` with no review directory writes `No review directory at ...` to stdout. A script piping it to a JSON parser fails. Emit a valid JSON document (empty rows, `missing_dir: true`) when `--json` is set. Alternatively, send the message to stderr.

findings.title: `UsageCapture(set())` makes callers supply the constructor's internal state
findings.description: Every caller passes an empty set for `warned`, and `review_client` passes a fresh `set()` to `resolve_cost` on each call. That means a pricing warning repeats on every standalone review. A default-constructed `UsageCapture()` would be simpler, and the dedupe set could be shared where the intent is once-per-alias.

findings.title: Alias table looked up once per cell render
findings.description: `_is_subscription` calls `get_all_aliases()` for every cost cell. This is harmless at current report sizes. Resolving it once per report would be cleaner.

findings.title: Usage capture design and test coverage
findings.description: Record construction is centralised in `UsageCapture` and `stamp`. The SDK usage reader treats malformed values defensively and logs a warning. The new tests cover success, failure, partial, cancellation, missing-capture, and state round-trip paths. I did not run the tests. The reorder of the `except ProviderError` branch in `dispatch.py` is safe: `ModelResolutionError`, `ModelPoolNotImplemented`, `ContextForgeError` and `ProjectRulesError` do not subclass `ProviderError`, and `DispatchStalledError` does.
